reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds (order 272: 8656, order 274: 1382). Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly (order 272: 8656, order 274: 1382), so I can proceed. Next I need the order list to identify which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders list has three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 62169 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme (62169) and birch (48740) are done. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders list, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.
Refunds match Alpha's report, and all three net balances reconcile with the orders minus refunds (acme 62169, birch 50122-1382=48740, cobalt 35333-8656=26677). Recording the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net balance (48740) matches orders minus refund 274, so I'll record its payout next.
Cobalt's net balance is 26677, which matches its orders (21885 + 13448 = 35333) minus refund 272 (8656). Acme and birch are already paid, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three net balances were paid, and each matches orders minus refunds. The refunds table matched Alpha's report before any payout was recorded, so the batch is complete.
